title: kith-core: add node_name to Identity for Contact bootstrap
description:
What: Add pub node_name: String to the Identity struct in kith-core so that Peer/deliver handlers can obtain the sender's MagicDNS hostname (needed for ContactStore::upsert peer_mailbox_host).

Algorithm:
1. Edit crates/kith-core/src/auth.rs: add pub node_name: String field to Identity struct (after display_name)
2. Update all Identity { ... } construction sites in kith-core tests to include node_name
3. Edit crates/kithd/src/auth.rs: populate node_name from WhoIsResponse.node.name when building Identity in authorize()
4. Edit crates/kithd/src/extractors.rs: populate node_name in Identity constructed in FromRequestParts impl
5. Update all Identity construction sites in kithd tests (auth.rs, extractors.rs, events.rs) to include node_name
6. Run: cargo test --workspace
7. Run: cargo clippy --all-features -- -D warnings

Defensive rules:
- node_name comes from WhoIs node.name (Tailscale MagicDNS, trusted); it is NOT from request body
- If node.name is empty, use empty string; callers must handle empty node_name gracefully (fallback to peer_user_id lookup)
- No PII (user_id) in log statements; node_name in logs is acceptable for debugging
- Do NOT normalize or parse node_name; store verbatim

Agent team: Researcher R reads Identity usage sites. Implementer I makes the additive change. Validator V runs full workspace test suite.

Tests:
- Condition: authorize() populates node_name from WhoIsNode.name; oracle: known WhoIsNode.name value in test fixture; assertion: identity.node_name == expected
- Condition: empty node.name stored verbatim; oracle: empty string literal; assertion: identity.node_name.is_empty()
